mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% for two consecutive months signals central bank over-tightening, which raises real discount rates and compresses equity present value, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% and remains > 0.3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: accelerating inflation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL decays below 0.3% within 10 days after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the expected discount rate on equities increases, reducing the present value of future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.25pp in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive during such FEDFUNDS hikes (t-test p < 0.05), or the effect is mediated by a concurrent equity risk premium surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) exceeding 20,000 for three consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 20,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such labor expansions (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when unemployment falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) falls by more than 2% in a month relative to the prior month, it signals weakening consumer demand, which elevates risk premia and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such declines (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% indicates supply-side weakness, lowering business confidence and investment expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥ 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during such supply shocks (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when inflation is also falling.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month moving averages by at least 2% each suggest a robust economic recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such dual series upswings (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is mediated by a simultaneous equity risk premium decline.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals a labor market softening that reduces wage growth expectations and compresses future earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during such labor market softening (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when unemployment falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (indicated by a 12-month average FEDFUNDS below 1%), the lower real interest rate environment supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is absent when equity risk premium falls.
